scope: Theorem A.4 (Bounded-printer uniformization) of the manuscript “An explicit power saving for the exact discrete Fourier transform” (preprints/An-explicit-power-saving-for-the-exact-discrete-Fourier-transform-September-25-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 130 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 670d0115ea2553e6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 28-29. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose a fixed bit machine prints a sequence of complete records (mt, Ct) with strictly increasing mt → ∞, where Ct computes Fmt by st = o(mt log mt) scalar linear gates. Each record must explicitly list the gates, output indices, and a scalar preparation program with every instruction explicitly listed and executed once in order. Its instructions use rational literals, field operations with valid nonzero divisors, and canonical Fourier roots ζa = exp(2πi/a) of positive integer orders whose orders are written literally in binary. Then 28 there is one deterministic algorithm computing every Fn in o(n log n) time, including preparation and indexing in the model of this paper. A single specified root of order less than 8n3 suffices.
